quotes.text: A golden path is an approved, repeatable route for a job that teams do often. It doesn't tell every developer how to write their code.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A crisp definition of golden paths that clarifies what they do and do not control.

quotes.text: If the platform says no without a route forward, people will build their own workarounds outside the platform. That creates the exact confusion the platform was meant to reduce.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains why golden paths need an escape hatch.

quotes.text: Good guardrails do not turn the platform into a ticket machine. They remove the slow approvals for normal work while keeping clear boundaries around access, security, and money.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Summarizes the purpose of guardrails in a self-service platform.

quotes.text: An IDP is not backstage or any other single portal product. A portal can be the screen people use, but the platform includes the people who maintain it, the standards they agree on
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Corrects the common myth that an IDP is just a portal.

quotes.text: Start small, pick one painful workflow, one team and one golden path. Listen before you build more.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Practical starting advice for introducing an IDP.

chapters.title: Why developers need a better way
IDP myths and where Azure fits

takeaways: An internal developer platform is a self-service front door to approved building blocks, run by a platform team that treats developers as customers.
Golden paths, a service catalog and guardrails built on Entra ID, Azure Policy and Key Vault let teams move fast without manual approvals or unsafe shortcuts.
An IDP is not a single portal product; start with one painful workflow and one golden path, then measure waiting time, tickets and developer feedback.
hook: Developers often spend more time on tickets, permissions and cloud setup than on the feature they were asked to build. This episode explains internal developer platforms in plain English for IT and engineering leaders, covering golden paths, service catalogs, guardrails and how Azure tools fit behind a single self-service request.
